doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Leaning toward jazz from the start
summary: Palmer says he always leaned toward jazz, playing blues and St. Louis Blues without music at Sylvan Beach.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: This music you were playing, when did you first get into what you would call a jazz band?

Well I always leaned towards playing jazz you know. I mean that was in Rome before I even went out. Because when I played with this black band in Sylvan Beach, that was without music. We played songs, and then we’d play what they call the blues you know, which was a traditional, three chord changes and so forth. St. Louis Blues was a standard and then we’d take off on it you know. Go ahead, ask me questions. I don’t want to talk too much.
